slides.title: What is an API?
slides.narration:
Today, we will learn about APIs.
This is a very important concept.
It helps you understand AI use.
An API is like a magic connector.
slides.image_prompt: Graphic of two abstract systems connecting, with a 'magic' light beam or sparkle between them.

slides.title: API: A Restaurant Waiter
slides.narration:
Let's use a simple analogy.
Imagine you are at a restaurant.
You want a delicious hamburger.
Your application is like you.
slides.image_prompt: Person sitting at a restaurant table, looking hungry, with thought bubble of a hamburger.

slides.title: The AI Model is the Kitchen
content: You don't go into the kitchen.
The kitchen (AI model) prepares your food.
slides.narration:
You don't go into the kitchen.
The kitchen is complex.
It prepares your food.
The AI model is like this kitchen.
It processes complex tasks.
slides.image_prompt: Busy kitchen scene, chefs cooking, representing a complex AI model.

slides.title: The API is the Waiter
content: You give your order (prompt) to a waiter (API).
The waiter takes it to the kitchen.
slides.narration:
Instead, you give your order.
This order is your prompt.
You give it to a waiter.
The waiter is the API.
He takes your order to the kitchen.
slides.image_prompt: Waiter taking an order from a customer at a table. Speech bubble above customer: 'I want a hamburger.'

slides.title: The AI's Response is the Dish
content: The waiter brings it back to you.
slides.narration:
The kitchen prepares your food.
Then, the waiter brings the dish.
He brings it back to your table.
The AI's response is this finished dish.
The API delivers it back to you.
slides.image_prompt: Waiter bringing a plate with a hamburger back to the customer.

slides.title: What is an API?
content: A messenger between your application and the AI model.
slides.narration:
So, an API is that waiter.
API means Application Programming Interface.
It acts as a messenger.
It connects your application to the AI model.
slides.image_prompt: Diagram: 'Your Application' -> 'API (Waiter icon)' -> 'AI Model (Kitchen icon)' -> 'API (Waiter icon)' -> 'Your Application'.

slides.title: How an API Works
content: Sends it to the AI model.
slides.narration:
The API takes your request.
It sends it to the AI model.
Then, it returns the model's response.
This is how AI services work.
It makes AI accessible.
slides.image_prompt: Animated diagram of the flow: request going in, processing, response coming out, clearly labeled.

slides.title: API Keys: Your Secret Password
content: Proves your permission to use the AI service.
slides.narration:
Now, let's talk about API Keys.
An API Key is a secret password.
It is like your unique ID card.
It proves you have permission.
Permission to use the AI service.
slides.image_prompt: A key icon with a lock, next to a text box that says 'API Key: **************' (masked).

slides.title: Keep Your API Key Private!
slides.narration:
This key identifies you.
It ensures secure access.
You must always keep your API key private.
Never share it with anyone.
It is very important for security.
slides.image_prompt: A warning sign (exclamation mark in a triangle) next to a blurred API key, with a 'DO NOT SHARE' message.

slides.title: API Requests: Placing Your Order
content: The act of placing your order.
Sending your API key and prompt to the AI service.
slides.narration:
Next, let's understand requests.
A request is placing your order.
In code, this means sending two things.
You send your API key.
And you send your prompt.
You send them to the AI service.
slides.image_prompt: A computer screen showing a simple code snippet sending an API request with an API key variable and a prompt string.

slides.title: API in Action
slides.narration:
So, your application uses the API key.
It sends your prompt as a request.
The API connects to the AI model.
The AI processes the request.
Then it sends back a response.
The API delivers it to your app.
slides.image_prompt: Flowchart showing 'Your Application' -> 'API (with API Key icon)' -> 'AI Model' -> 'API (with Response icon)' -> 'Your Application'.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, we learned about APIs.
We used the waiter analogy.
We understood API Keys.
And we learned about API requests.
These are vital for using AI.
